f2.decision_a_correct: yes, acceptable: it keeps standing asserted by the assessment (may_back_model_claim_verdict blesses it), does not re-attribute a model's assessment to the miner, and is fail-closed; the mining provenance is genuinely rendered, so the masking is removed rather than moved
f2.argument_against_a: claim.producer='model' still reads as 'this material is model-sourced' to any reader or consumer that does not parse the free-text reason, and generated_by.producer='replay' contradicts it at the docket level; the correction lives in prose, not in a typed field
f2.argument_against_b: miner-keyed provenance would report producer='replay' for a claim whose CONFIRMS was asserted by a model, hiding who asserted standing and conflating 'who mined it' with 'who blessed it' - it re-attributes a model's assessment to the miner and loses the standing information (and would look like a cap/downgrade)
f2.alternative_c: two distinct typed fields - e.g. claim.producer (assessing authority, as now) plus claim.mined_by (mining provenance) - or a nested {assessed_by, mined_by} object; strictly better for machine readers, at the cost of a schema change (the Claim model is extra='forbid', so an added optional field is backward-compatible for reads but changes the rendered shape and needs a schema decision)
f2.cost_of_two_part_statement: the second half of the statement is carried in a free-text `verdict_reason` whose documented meaning (manifest.py:155-163, unedited because manifest.py was not touched) is 'non-None ONLY when a declared standing was capped below CONFIRMS'. After U5.19, verdict_reason is non-None for a CONFIRMS claim with no cap, so `verdict_reason != null` is no longer a reliable downgrade marker; any consumer that treated it as one now sees a contradiction, and the note is unparseable prose. This is the concrete cost of option (a) as implemented.
